patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Hunter and Kaspr share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose Hunter only if your buying job matches “Domain email finder, verifier, and cold email sequences (All-in-one) — Free 50 credits; St” rather than Kaspr's shape. Choose Kaspr only if your buying job matches “LinkedIn-centric EU/EMEA B2B contact capture (Chrome) — Free plan; Starter from $49/mo ann” rather than Hunter's shape. Workflow advantage: Hunter leans email-outreach; Kaspr leans lead-management. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Hunter and Kaspr share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Hunter is Domain email finder, verifier, and cold email sequences (All-in-one) — Free 50 credits; Starter from $49/mo.; Kaspr is LinkedIn-centric EU/EMEA B2B contact capture (Chrome) — Free plan; Starter from $49/mo annual headline..
- Company-size focus: Hunter (micro, small-business, mid-market) vs Kaspr (small-business, mid-market).
- Workflow coverage skew: Hunter-leaning email-outreach vs Kaspr-leaning lead-management.
- Researched limits: Hunter — Contact data is email/domain-centric — weaker as a full phone+firmographic mega-database; Kaspr — LinkedIn-centric capture — coverage and compliance depend on LinkedIn workflow policies.

Limitations — Hunter: Contact data is email/domain-centric — weaker as a full phone+firmographic mega-database; Lead scoring is limited versus enterprise SI platforms; Kaspr: LinkedIn-centric capture — coverage and compliance depend on LinkedIn workflow policies; Native email outreach/sequencing depth is limited versus engagement platforms.

Poor-fit cases: Hunter is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Contact data is email/domain-centric — weaker as a full phone+firmographic mega-database · Kaspr is a poor fit when that limitation bites: LinkedIn-centric capture — coverage and compliance depend on LinkedIn workflow policies · Avoid Hunter if you actually need Kaspr's motion (LinkedIn-centric EU/EMEA B2B contact capture (Chrome) — Free plan; Starter from )

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
